A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we develop three novel wavelets domain denoising algorithms, which are subband-adaptive (for single-band denoising), spatially-adaptive, and multivalued, which are all based on estimating a signal probability.
we have developed a new wavelet denoising framework that is able to exploit both spatial and multispectral information for image denoising.
the proposed methods are more robust and adaptive than the existing methods in terms of mean square error, while the computational complexity of our methods is comparable to that of existing ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper modeling of the probability that the wavelet coefficients contain a noise-free signal component is essential for the design of efficient denoising schemes.

the proposed approach is a general framework for multiresolution single-band, multiband, spatially adaptive, and subband-adaptive image denoising, which is based on the estimation of a single quantity, i.e. the probability of presence of the signal of interest in each coefficient.
the estimation of signal of interest probability in wavelet domain image denoising is crucial to improve performance and to reduce the complexity of the denoising process.
